newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds were chalking up a stronger intraday close late Friday afternoon as debt market players cheered news of the Reserve Bank's $1.5 billion revolving credit facility and a home loan rate cut by a local bank.
The benchmark R150 bond was last quoted at 14.645 percent from 14.71 percent late on Thursday and roughly in line with last Friday's close.

The Reserve Bank's facility, announced late Thursday was perceived as significantly boosting its ability to halt any significant capital outflows in the wake of the July 1 easing of foreign exchange controls on individuals.
"I think there's a growing perception that what's going to happen on July 1 won't be as enourmous as people had previously anticipated," said Securities Investment Bank director Chris Greyling.
He added Standard Bank's decision to cut its fixed and capped home loan rates also rubbed some shine into local debt.

"It's not a major thing but I think it's the first crack in the dam wall so to speak and what'll happen is that the other banks will follow suit over the next few months. I think it will pave the way for further reductions," he said.
The R150 had opened strongly on Friday going on to thumb its nose over lunch at the rise in average yields for the government's weekly T-bill tender.
"Over the day we saw a little short-covering and institutional demand for call options as well," noted one Johannesburg-based dealer.
In forex dealings the rand meandered through a quiet local session to sit mildly firmer by the close.
The local unit was last at 4.5065/5095 against the dollar from 4.5110/5140 overnight, hovering above its intraday best of 4.5060.
"It was extremely quiet. We saw good interest to sell dollars early in the morning on the back of the $1.5 billion credit facility," said one trader.
"We saw a bit of demand at the 4.5050 level and the rand dipped to the current levels which is where it stayed all afternoon."
Rand traders agreed with their debt counterparts that the central bank's loan boded well for market resilience from July 1.

"It's definitely improved the market. For July 1 there is going to be small pressure but now I don't think to the same extent as what a lot of people were thinking. I don't think we're going to see any screaming up of the rand now," said one.
The unit's range over next week was pegged between 4.5050 and 4.5200 rand to the dollar.

Both bond and forex markets glossed over the Reserve Bank's Quarterly Bulletin, released late on Thursday, which gave a mixed reading on the economy with the main implication that an early interest rate cut was not on the cards, given a strong performance by the manufacturing sector.

Against the crosses the rand had a mixed day and was last at 25.4090/4269 against the yen from 25.2503/2893 on Thursday, at 0.3838/3842 marks from 0.3823/3827 marks and at 7.4574/4653 against sterling from 7.4219/4332 previously.
On the money market, short-term rates were unchanged with three-month NCDs quoted at 16.05 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate also steady at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage fell to 7.008 billion rand on Thursday from 7.314 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg Newsroom +27 11 482-1003
